picks.blurb: College Football Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 PM Get Ready for the Texas Tech Red Raiders vs. TCU Horned Frogs Showdown – Your Ultimate Game Preview Presented by Visit Lubbock. Share Traveling in for the game? Visit Lubbock has you covered for Things to Do, Can’t Miss Experiences and Where to Stay! On June 8, Sonny Dykes was certainly concerned about what was happening in the Brendan Sorsby saga, calling it a “bad day for college football.” Dykes doubled down in an interview with ESPN, asking, “How is anyone ever going to trust the outcome of a game again?” According to ESPN’s write-up, another of Dykes’ “key worries” was that his players might think betting on football was “allowable” because Sorsby had seemingly gotten out of the situation with just a slap on the wrist. “I think it's a shame. Everyone is looking out for their self-interests. No one is looking out for what's right in college football,” Dykes said. Maybe, just maybe, Sonny Dykes' key worries this offseason should have been about his own team instead of what was happening in Lubbock. Fresh off what I'm sure was an incredible offseason of practices, one of his prized transfer portal additions sucker-punched a starting wide receiver and sent him to the hospital just before the Horned Frogs traveled to Ireland, where they lost to a team they dominated the previous season. Despite starting 0-1, the Horned Frogs continued putting together great weeks of practice while losing half their games. They did manage to beat Baylor, ultimately contributing to Dave Aranda's firing. I mean, how could anyone lose to this terrible TCU offense? The same offense Dykes was so worried about. Not even the incredible weekly practices could save the Horned Frogs from falling to 5-5. A 21-point fourth-quarter surge by Utah gave TCU their 6th loss of the season, and with an apathetic fan base and an offense averaging just 18.4 points per game in Big 12 play, Dykes was fired before he could make the trip home to Lubbock for Thanksgiving. Interim coach Andy Avalos has his defense playing well, allowing just 20.8 points per game. That unit should provide a test for Mack Leftwich and the Red Raiders, who are averaging 36.6 points per game in Big 12 play. Texas Tech is clearly the better team in 2026. The Red Raiders have a head coach, a quality offense and a defense rounding into form at the right time. They also have some extra motivation. There's the offseason commentary from Dykes and athletic director Mike Buddie, but there's also the matter of the Saddle. TCU took it in 2024 and has held it for two seasons after the teams didn't meet in 2025. Texas Tech has won just once in the last six meetings between the programs. The Red Raiders are 13.5-point favorites on thanksgiving and the game should play out accordingly. Texas Tech needs a win to clinch a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game and keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. But there's another piece of business to take care of: getting that dadgum Saddle back. I don't expect an outrageous shootout. In fact, I think this game looks a lot like the Baylor matchup. Still, I'll take Texas Tech to win and cover. If there's a game in which the Red Raiders should want to make a statement, it's Thanksgiving night against the Horned Frogs. Even with the students being home for the holiday, the Red Raiders should fill the Galaxy more than TCU in a season opener. Traveling in for the game? away.blurb: TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah The TCU Horned Frogs face a massive hurdle ahead of Saturday's showdown against the No. 2 Utah Utes. Starting quarterback Jaden Craig landed on Friday night's Big 12 availability report as doubtful, putting sophomore backup Adam Schobel in line to make his first career start, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. TCU listed Craig as probable earlier in the week before downgrading him Friday night. Losing Craig deals a major blow to a 5-5 Horned Frogs offense chasing bowl eligibility against an undefeated 10-0 Utah squad. The Harvard transfer ranks third in the Big 12 with 266.4 passing yards per game, completing 223 of 344 throws for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions while adding four rushing scores. Against Kansas State last Saturday, Craig went 20-for-34 for 225 yards and a touchdown without throwing a pick. Now, the spotlight shifts to Schobel. The 6-foot-5 former four-star recruit from Columbus, Texas, has seen limited action across three appearances this season. He threw one incomplete pass against the Grambling Tigers in September and logged four carries for 11 yards, including three rushes for three yards against Kansas State. TCU's injury woes extend beyond the quarterback room. The Horned Frogs also ruled out running back G'Ivori Graham and linebacker Keylan Abrams for Saturday's contest in Fort Worth, though defensive tackles Markis Deal and Ansel Din-Mbuh alongside edge rusher Cheta Ofili remain probable. Meanwhile, Utah ruled out safety Marcus Wimberly and listed long snapper Logan Castor as questionable. Throwing a first-time starter against the Big 12's top team is no easy task, but Schobel gets his shot to shock college football under the Fort Worth lights. home.blurb: Last week in the Cardinals' sluggish win over Stetson, UofL was without their starting shooting guard, Seth Trimble. Leading up to the game, reports said Trimble would miss it with a “minor injury,” and they expected him to be available Tuesday for Louisville’s matchup with Texas Tech. After gaining eligibility through the “five-for-five rule,” Trimble was one of Kelsey’s biggest additions from the Transfer Portal. He has started in every game this year, except vs. Stetson, when he was out, and with Louisville looking to pull off the upset, the UNC transfer will have to be healthy. The good news is that Trimble sounds like he will play in this huge rank-vs-rank matchup, and he is trending toward a return. Thanksgiving week is here, which means Louisville basketball’s Players Era 16 run is about to start. The Cardinals are currently in Las Vegas, where they are scheduled to tip off Tuesday, Nov. 24, for their first matchup of the event. Pat Kelsey challenges Flory Bidunga to become a centerpiece of Louisville's offense The Cards will look to secure their first marquee win of the season, as they face No. 9 Texas Tech. UofL enters this matchup 3-1, including their recent 83-69 win over Stetson. Pat Kelsey has struggled against ranked teams in the past, and tomorrow’s matchup will be a big test for this Lousiville squad. On Sunday, the Cardinals held a virtual press conference ahead of their game against Texas Tech, and Louisville fans got the Seth Trimble injury update they wanted. Seth Trimble is expected to play Tuesday against Texas Tech On Sunday, Kelsey confirmed the report is still accurate, as the Cardinals' head coach expects the UNC transfer to play. "Seth, we expect him to play," stated Kelsey. The Cardinals will need Trimble on Tuesday to pull off this upset, as the UNC transfer is a key piece to Kelsey’s offense and defense. He is a physical guard who will defend the opposing team’s best guard and will force turnovers, as he is averaging 1.7 steals per game, including two steals in each of the past two games. In addition to his defense, he is an offensive threat, averaging 13.3 points per game, the third-highest on the team, behind Flory Bidunga and Adrian Wooley. Trimble spent his first four seasons at North Carolina, including last season, when he averaged 14.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. The Cardinals have just a 29% chance of winning, according to ESPN Analytics, as the Red Raiders enter this game 5-0. Texas Tech already has a marquee win this season after the Red Raiders defeated No. 3 Illinois 84-78. Louisville and Texas Tech are set to play Tuesday, Nov. 24 at 8 p.m. ET inside Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Florida State Seminoles will attempt to become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023 and wrap up their ACC schedule with a .500 record when they host the NC State Wolfpack at Doak Campbell Stadium Saturday afternoon. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on the ACCN. FSU will celebrate its annual Homecoming and Seminole Heritage game and will wear turquoise jerseys and pants for the first time in program history. FSU is 3-0 in Heritage games and 63-12-1 all-time on Homecoming, with 12 consecutive victories. Throughout Native American communities, turquoise represents harmony, friendship and fellowship. The team found out it would wear the jerseys Sunday when defensive back Zae Thomas, a member of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, displayed the uniforms in the team meeting. For more information on FSU’s unique relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and Seminole Heritage, visit noles.co/Heritage. Florida State football to wear new uniform combination against NC State to honor Seminole Heritage Florida State (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and NC State will meet for the 45th time, with the Noles leading the series, 27-17, including a 16-6 record in Doak. However, NC State has won the last four matchups with Florida State and six of the last seven meetings. Last year, the 11-21 loss at NC State likely cost the 5-win Seminoles the opportunity to become bowl eligible. Under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, the Seminoles will attempt to win their third consecutive game before closing out the season against the Florida Gators at home on Black Friday afternoon, again with another short week to prepare. The last time FSU won 3 straight games was to open the 2025 season before then losing 7 of the next 9 games. The Wolfpack (4-6, 2-5 ACC) also fired their head coach, Dave Doeren, midseason, ending his 14-year tenure as the winningest coach in Wolfpack history, compiling a 98-74 overall record, including 11 bowl appearances and 10 winning seasons. Former NFL quarterback and former Chuck Amato-coached NC State alum, Phillip Rivers, bringing six years’ experience as a Catholic high school football head coach, was officially hired as the new head coach for NC State earlier this week, effective next season. It has been reported that he will travel to Tallahassee along with the Wolfpack team. Rivers signed a reported five-year deal starting at $3.25 million in total compensation for his first year ($2.4375 million base salary plus $812,500 in supplemental income). This is roughly half of Doeren’s previous $6.375 million salary, making Rivers one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches. NC State’s interim head coach Todd Goebbel led the team to a 31–10 win over California before suffering a 41–3 blowout loss to Duke and a 34–31 collapse against Syracuse, where the Wolfpack blew an 11-point lead in the final five minutes. Junior 6’6” quarterback CJ Bailey Jr. has completed 186 of his 295 passes attempted for 2,289 yards with 14 TDs and 5 interceptions. Sophomore quarterback Will Wilson, who has only completed 9 of 12 passes for 35 yards, has scored 8 rushing touchdowns for the Wolfpack during his time behind center despite NC State starting seven different lineup combinations on the offensive line in their 10 games due to injuries. Sophomore running back Jayden “Duke” Scott leads the team in rushing with 504 yards on 81 attempts for a 6.22 yard/rush average, along with 5 touchdowns. On defense, linebacker Popo Aguirre leads the team in tackles with 85, followed by CB Brian Nelson II with 47. LB Elijah Satchell leads the team in sacks with five. In their last outing, FSU wrapped up their road schedule with arguably their best defensive performance of the season so far, a 16-10 win at Pittsburgh, under interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims. FSU’s defense held Pitt, previously ranked 24th in total offense (446), to just 306 total yards, or 140 yards below their season average. The Noles defense allowed only 10 points to the Panthers, 22 points fewer than Pitt’s season average of 31.9 points/game, forced a crucial fourth-and-one turnover on downs in the third quarter, deflected six passes, recorded an interception, and sealed the game with a 4th-down stop on Pitt’s final drive. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 26 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Panikowski accounted for 23 points in the two road wins. He became the first FBS player since 2023 with a touchdown, field goal, and 4+ extra points in the win at BC before kicking a season-high three field goals at Pitt. His 47-yarder against Pitt was a season-long. FSU TE Corbyn Fordham is the younger brother of NC State linebacker Caden Fordham, who played against FSU in 2025 and recorded 15 tackles for NC State. away.headline: Florida shares injury update for star WR Vernell Brown III
away.blurb: Florida put out and official injury update on the star pass catcher Tuesday afternoon, saying that Brown has opted to undergo surgery on his injured knee. Per the statement, the procedure is expected to solve the lingering issue for good, but it will also keep him on the shelf for the “immediate future.” A 5-star recruit in the 2025 cycle, Brown became one of the biggest recruiting wins for the Gators in recent memory when he chose Florida over several other big name schools. He put together a solid freshman season under former head coach Billy Napier before breaking out during Florida's first 4 games of the 2026 campaign, becoming the primary target for quarterback Aaron Philo during that early stretch. He hauled in 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 touchdowns before suffering the aforementioned knee injury during the Gators' Week 4 win against Ole Miss, missing several weeks as a result. It initially looked like Brown would be able to return for Florida's matchup against Georgia , but he ended up reaggravating the injury during the bye week prolonged his absence. He'll be out this week. He's not going to play,” Sumrall said. “He's dying to play. It's an unfortunate deal.” “It was substantial enough that we knew it would put him on the shelf for a little while,” Sumrall said. “Maybe a week, two, three weeks, didn't really know. But felt like there would be a timetable to return that wouldn't be terribly long.” Brown continued to reappear on the injury report in the weeks that followed. Coming out of the bye week, Sumrall said, Brown “practiced really good on Monday and Tuesday” before reinjuring his knee in a non-contact incident during Wednesday practice in Week 9, forcing him to miss Florida's matchup against Georgia. Before the Gators' 34-27 win against Vanderbilt on Saturday, Sumrall appeared unsure about Brown's return to the field. “It's hurting him as much as anybody. He wants to play. He cares. He's a Gator,” Sumrall said. “Can't wait to watch him get back on the field. He makes everyone around him better. He's a quarterback's best friend. You get him the ball in space and he makes things happen. But he will not be available this week.” Listen & Schedule Listen & Schedule The sophomore first appeared on the injury report after suffering a knee strain in the second quarter of Florida's Week 4 win against Ole Miss. Sumrall said the injury wasn't a ligament tear, but it was significant. “Wednesday he had a non-contact setback where he was just running a route down the field in our indoor facility,” Sumrall said. “And it tweaked on him.” The rivalry matchup against Florida State will mark the eighth game Brown has missed this season. “I'm hopeful he can play, yeah. away.blurb: Northwestern's defense could be getting some much-needed help as the Wildcats prepare for their matchup against Minnesota on Saturday. Defensive backs Josh Fussell and Ore Adeyi are both listed as questionable on the latest availability report, giving Northwestern some reason for optimism heading into the weekend. Fussell's potential return would be especially important for the Wildcats. The defensive back has been sidelined since the Indiana game on Sept. 25 and has been a significant absence in Northwestern's secondary. He is one of the team's key defensive players, and getting him back on the field would provide a major boost to a defense that has dealt with several injuries throughout the season. Fussell has been missed over the past several weeks, particularly with Northwestern facing some of the more explosive offenses in the Big Ten. His potential return would give the Wildcats another experienced option in the secondary and could help improve their coverage and overall defensive communication. Adeyi is another important name to watch. He went down with an injury during Northwestern's loss to Ohio State . Seeing him listed as questionable rather than out is an encouraging development, although his availability will ultimately depend on how he progresses before Saturday. Having both players potentially available would be a significant development for a Northwestern defense that needs all the help it can get. The Wildcats have shown an ability to create turnovers and make important plays defensively, but they have also struggled to contain explosive plays and prevent opponents from putting together big drives. Fussell and Adeyi potentially returning would be a positive step in the right direction. Neither player is officially confirmed to play, but having both listed as questionable gives Northwestern some hope of getting key contributors back. home.headline: Ryan Hopkins headlines first Wisconsin vs. Purdue availability report
home.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Charles Woodson (2) and Archie Griffin (45) are two key figures in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry. Arguably the greatest rivalry in all of sports returns in Week 13 of the college football season, with Ohio State hosting Michigan at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, at noon ET (FOX) on Saturday, Nov. 28. This year's edition of the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry , known simply as The Game, is different from recent years, with both programs enduring down seasons and neither contending for a national championship. Some would argue that makes this the purest version of the rivalry, with both teams fueled by their dislike for each other and little else. Ohio State is a 10.5-point favorite, and my college football picks back the Buckeyes to win big. Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry history: The Game Wins (official; six ties) 9 (1901-1909) Longest win streak 8 (2012-2019) Largest margin of victory 1027-367-36 (.731) Program record 997-342-53 (.735) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Few rivalries feature two teams as successful as Michigan and Ohio State . That history makes their mutual hatred even more intense. The Wolverines and the Buckeyes have both won plenty of national championships, produced multiple Heisman Trophy winners, and sent countless players to the NFL, but more than anything else, they take pride in beating each other. This rivalry is built as much on program success as it is on animosity. Michigan has more wins than any other program in college football history, and Ohio State has a higher winning percentage than any other program in college football history. The Game often has major implications for the national championship and the Heisman Trophy race. It all began in 1897, and The Game has been played every season since 1918, except in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Its history stretches from Fielding Yost's early dominance through Woody Hayes and Bo Schembechler's Ten-Year War, Jim Tressel and Urban Meyer's successful runs, and Jim Harbaugh's revival of Michigan. This is the college football rivalry. Recent Michigan-Ohio State results Nov. 29, 2025 27-9 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9.5) Nov. 30, 2024 13-10 (Michigan) Michigan (+19.5) Nov. 25, 2023 30-24 (Michigan) Michigan (-3.5) Nov. 26, 2022 45-23 (Michigan) Michigan (+8.5) Nov. 27, 2021 42-27 (Michigan) Michigan (+7) Nov. 30, 2019 56-27 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-9) Nov. 24, 2018 62-39 (Ohio State) Ohio State (+3.5) Nov. 25, 2017 31-20 (Ohio State) Michigan (+12.5) Nov. 26, 2016 30-27 (Ohio State) Michigan (+4.5) Nov. 28, 2015 42-13 (Ohio State) Ohio State (-1.5) History of the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry When did the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry start? The Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry began in 1897 and was immediately a natural rivalry because of the bordering states' history with the Toledo War (a boundary dispute between the states over the Toledo Strip). The Wolverines won the first matchup on Oct. 16, 1897, in Ann Arbor, 34-0. The programs didn't meet again until a 0-0 tie in 1900, then played every season through 1912. Michigan went 12-0-2 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1912. The Buckeyes didn't win The Game for the first time until 1919, beating Michigan 13-3 to spark a three-game winning streak. However, Michigan owned the rivalry, for the most part, until Hayes arrived in 1951. The Wolverines went 32-12-4 against Ohio State from 1897 to 1950. Why is it called The Game? Michigan vs. Ohio State is known to most as The Game because of its importance to both fan bases and college football nationally. The matchup has closed out the regular season since 1935, and usually there's plenty on the line when these teams meet. Before Big Ten expansion, the winner of The Game would frequently win the conference and head to the Rose Bowl for a chance at a national title. And in later years, The Game would play a key role in setting the Big Ten Championship Game matchup. The loser of The Game generally considers the season a disappointment. What was the Ten-Year War? What kicked off the Ten-Year War between Michigan and Ohio State was the Wolverines hiring Hayes' protege, Schembechler, in 1969. Schembechler had been an assistant under Hayes at Ohio State from 1958 to 1962 before following in Hayes' footsteps and becoming head coach at Miami (OH). Both Hayes (1949-1950) and Schembechler (1963-1968) coached at Miami (Ohio) before taking over Ohio State and Michigan. Hayes went 12-6 against Michigan in The Game from 1951-1968 and flipped the once maize and blue-dominated rivalry to the scarlet and grey. That led Michigan in a new direction with the hiring of Schembechler, who immediately made his presence felt. In Schembechler's first game against Ohio State, Michigan pulled off "the upset of the century" by beating the No. 1 Buckeyes 24-12 and ending their 22-game winning streak. That victory marked the beginning of the Ten-Year War. From 1970 to 1975, in four of the six meetings, both Ohio State and Michigan were ranked in the top five. During the Ten-Year War, the programs shared the Big Ten title multiple times, with Michigan ultimately having the upper hand, going 5-4-1 against Ohio State. The war ended after the 1978 season, when Hayes was fired for punching Clemson linebacker Charlie Bauman after an interception in the Gator Bowl. It was during the Ten-Year War that Ohio State began its tradition of referring to Michigan as "That Team Up North" when Hayes referred to the Wolverines as such. Best moments in the Michigan vs Ohio State rivalry The Snow Bowl (1950) Among the most famous games in the Michigan vs. Ohio State rivalry, the Snow Bowl was exactly what it sounds like: a game in a blizzard. The blizzard was so bad that the Buckeyes were given the option to cancel the game (they would have won the Big Ten title by default if they had), but Ohio State wanted to play its rival. All in all, the teams combined to punt the ball 45 times, with many of the punts coming on first down as they battled for field position and hoped the other team would fumble. Michigan would block two punts, one resulting in a safety and the other a touchdown, to win 9-3. The Wolverines didn't complete a single pass or gain a single first down, but took home the Big Ten title with the win. Ohio State head coach Wes Fesler would resign after the loss, leading to Hayes being hired. The Upset of the Century (1969) In Schembechler's first game against his former boss, Michigan would upset undefeated No. 1-ranked Ohio State 24-12. The Buckeyes were riding a 22-game winning streak and gunning for their second straight national title, but an all-time performance from Barry Pierson (three interceptions and a 60-yard punt return that set up a touchdown) would end Ohio State's shot at a championship. Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer is concerned about the Buckeyes heading into their game against Michigan Getty Michael Gallagher · HEAVY Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:25 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 29: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines is pursued by Kenyatta Jackson Jr. #97 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the fourth quarter at Michigan Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Duke vs North Carolina in basketball gets played at least twice. With Michigan and Ohio State, you have two behemoth universities from two different states, and it all comes down to this one game that, when it's at its biggest and best, stops the sports world cold. This isn't at its biggest and best this year, which means it's all about the rivalry. Trust me, you can be Michigan or Ohio State and win the national title, but if you don't beat the other, the season has a hole in it. Michigan finally got bowl-eligible with its thrilling win over UCLA last week. Ohio State won 27-9 last year to break a run of four straight Michigan wins. The Buckeyes haven't beaten the Wolverines in Columbus since 2018. How To Watch Michigan vs Ohio State Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Ohio Stadium, Columbus, OH – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Michigan Will Win The defense continues to be a force. It's ninth in the nation overall, with a nasty run defense that held up well against both UCLA's pounding style last week and Oregon's flash and speed before that. Rutgers is the only team to average more than four yards per carry against this Wolverine bunch. Ohio State's running game isn't good enough to carry the team. This is about as simple as it gets for a Wolverine team without a steady passing game. Run the ball well, force field goals, repeat. The Michigan ground attack hasn't been too bad, and in this, it just has to keep the clock moving – having Bryce Underwood under center should help. Ohio State is 1-4 when allowing over 85 rushing yards. Michigan is 6-2 when running for more than 80. But … Why Ohio State Will Win The Michigan passing attack is just plain putrid. It actually worked against Iowa, of all teams, but it's wildly inconsistent and doesn't do a thing downfield. Ohio State has to get up fast. It was able to do it in the 41-28 loss to Oregon, and scored first last week against Nebraska. Positive momentum will be everything to this Buckeye bunch. It won't have a problem if Michigan tries to keep running, but it does have to keep Underwood from finding a passing groove. The Buckeyes are now 0-4 against teams that connect on more than 60% of their passes. Underwood is hitting just 55% of his throws on the year. Michigan vs Ohio State Prediction, Betting Lines Will Jeremiah Smith do enough to take home the Heisman? This is his one final chance to make his case, and Michigan will have him wrapped up tight. The star caught three passes for 40 yards and a key score in last year's Buckeye win, and made five grabs for 35 yards and a touchdown in 2024. Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey will have another nice game – he hasn't been the problem in this rough run over the last month. He'll hit one deep shot to Smith, and that will be about enough. The Buckeye offense won't be anything pretty, but it'll get just enough points off a few scoring drives to hold up. Ohio State's defense will finally have a solid game again, but that's more because Michigan's offense just won't move. It's Michigan vs Ohio State. Forget everything else – it just means more. This year's edition of the game won't be up there in terms of implications , but neither team wants to lose to the other. Both teams are eliminated from winning the Big Ten and making the College Football Playoff, which will be the first season that neither team is in the playoff since 2018. It's been a parity-filled season of football and both the Wolverines and Buckeyes are on the wrong side of things. Michigan is coming off a massive home win against previously unbeaten UCLA. The Wolverines took the Bruins into triple overtime and Bryce Underwood found Jalen Hoffman in the corner of the end zone to win the game. Ohio State, however, faltered once again and has now lost three of its last four games. This time, to Nebraska on the road. Michigan's odds of beating Ohio State USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect In the last four games, Michigan has gone 2-2 with losses to both Michigan State and Oregon. While the Buckeyes are 1-3 with losses against USC, Oregon, and Nebraska. Neither team is playing well, but boh teams are playing poorly in different areas. Even so, ESPN's FPI isn't giving Michigan much of a chance to go on the road and win the game. The Wolverines have just a 10.8% chance to beating the Buckeyes this weekend, per the advanced analytics. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , Ohio State opened as a 14-point favorite, but the Buckeyes are now a 10-point favorite to beat Michigan. Which means some money has gone on the Wolverines recently. Two teams with two different faults Saturday will be a battle between good on good and bad on bad. Michigan's offense remains difficult to watch, although running back Savion Hiter has been a glimmer of hope in the last two weeks, rushing for over 100 yards. Ohio State's defense has really come apart and has allowed 30, 41, 31 points, respectively, in its last three losses. So we will see which unit can be slightly better on Saturday. And it's a different story on the other side of the ball. The Buckeyes might be playing backup quarterback Luke Fahey, but Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith, who can win in triple coverage. Michigan will have its hands full defending him on Saturday, but clearly, the Wolverines' strength is their defense. Can Michigan's defense win the game this weekend? If the Wolverines do win, it will be because Jay Hill and Co. get the job done. Samantha Madar/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Brandon Little · AtoZ Sports Mon, November 23, 2026 at 3:20 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The spread for the regular season finale between Ohio State and Michigan is a bit surprising. The Ohio State Buckeyes' College Football Playoff hopes are over after losing to Nebraska in Week 12. Now the only goal left for Ohio State in the 2026 season is beating the Michigan Wolverines , and the oddsmakers believe the Buckeyes will get it done comfortably. Ohio State sits at 7-4, just one game better than Michigan at 6-5. The Wolverines have been bad for most of this season. However, they just picked up their best win of the year, knocking off No. 4 UCLA in a triple-overtime game. QB Bryce Underwood returned as the starter, and Michigan leaned on the ground game and a strong defense to snap a two-game losing skid. Neither team is playing meaningful postseason games this year. For Ohio State, finishing 8-4 would be a big disappointment. Still, beating Michigan is something the Buckeyes need to do to at least end the season on the right foot. Ohio State is a double-digit favorite against Michigan According to FanDuel, Ohio State is a 10.5-point favorite against Michigan at the time of this article. That's a bold spread given what the Buckeyes have looked like since their Week 7 win over Indiana. Georgia (28%), Notre Dame (15%) and Texas (12%) have the best chances to win the college football national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 22, 2026). Coming out of a bye, Ohio State lost 30-18 in Week 9. The Buckeyes followed that up with a 41-28 loss to Oregon in Week 10. Even the win over Northwestern in Week 11 was far from convincing at 28-19. From there, Ohio State lost by three points on the road at Nebraska. The Buckeyes do return home for this one, and that helps their case. Ohio State is 5-1 at home this season, while Michigan is 1-2 in road games. Even so, laying 10.5 points with this version of the Buckeyes is a lot to ask, in my opinion. If I were betting on it, I would take Michigan to cover. Ohio State hasn't won a game by more than 10 points since its Week 6 win over Maryland. That's a long stretch for a team being asked to win by double digits in a rivalry game. The Ohio State vs Michigan rivalry is usually close Ohio State and Michigan typically play close games. The Buckeyes did get back in the win column in the rivalry last season with a 27-9 win in Ann Arbor, but one comfortable result doesn't change the history of how tight these games often are. Neither team is operating with a strong offense right now. The Wolverines are winning with their run game and defense, which is the kind of formula that keeps a game close and makes a double-digit spread tough to cover. Don't sleep on Michigan's ability to shorten this game and make it a grind. Ohio State does have the most dangerous player on the field. Jeremiah Smith gives the Buckeyes an edge that Michigan simply doesn't have on offense. Jeremiah Smith has a chance to lock down the Heisman Trophy This game will be a chance for Smith to all but lock down the Heisman Trophy. He has 1,482 receiving yards and 17 touchdown catches this season for the Buckeyes. A big performance against Michigan on the final weekend of the regular season would be the perfect way to cap off that kind of year. For the Buckeyes, the season hasn't gone the way anyone expected. Smith's production has been one of the few constants for an offense that has struggled to put teams away. At least according to the oddsmakers, Ohio State is going to go out and win this game in Week 13 to close out the regular season. Whether the Buckeyes can win it by more than 10 points is another question entirely. Time will tell if the oddsmakers or the recent results have it right. Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. Roughly 45 minutes later, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported that Underwood suffered a lower-body injury in the win over UCLA that left his status in question for Saturday’s game. Soon after, national reporters from On3 and ESPN confirmed the injury to Underwood. The quarterback appeared fine physically as he spoke to the press after the game on Saturday, calling it “a blessing” to get a second chance at being the Wolverines’ starting quarterback. Michigan will be required to submit a player availability report to the Big Ten beginning on Wednesday, with updates expected daily leading up to Saturday’s game in Columbus. RELATED: Michigan football a double-digit underdog vs. Ohio State In seven starts this season, Underwood has completed 54 percent of his throws for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, with six interceptions and two fumbles lost. Turnovers got him benched during a Week 6 win over Penn State, opening the door for freshman Tommy Carr to take over.

away.headline: Blake Frazer, Rod Moore, Andrew Marsh Headline Michigan's Initial Injury Report vs. UCLA
away.blurb: We knew that JJ Buchanan was going to be out. Kyle Whittingham said so on Monday, but it's very concerning to see the likes of Andrew Marsh, and even Channing Goodwin to a certain extent on the list. Without Buchanan, Marsh is the certified alpha on the team and will be a key part of the Wolverines' passing attack — especially if there is any hope to get it going. And the offensive line remains a major issue. Blake Frazier is now officially out and the Wolverines played without him last weekend. Brady Norton is questionable, too, and the Wolverines could opt to play both Manuel Beigel and Marky Walbridge once again this weekend. After back-to-back losses to Michigan State and Oregon, the Wolverines are looking to get back in the win column. In fact, Michigan needs one more win in the last two weeks in order to go bowling. The Wolverines haven't missed a bowl game since 2014, the final year of Brady Hoke in Ann Arbor. If Michigan is going to gain bowl eligibility this weekend, the Wolverines are going to have to earn it. Michigan will host UCLA, which hasn't lost a game all year. The Bruins are one of the most surprising teams in college football. Despite losing Nico Iamaleava for the season, Bob Chesney has turned to his backup quarterback, but it's only resulted in success. If the Wolverines are going to beat UCLA , it's going to have to get the job done without a few players. Here's how Michigan's initial availability report looks heading into the Wolverines' Week 12 game against UCLA. More concern regarding the offense Michigan will also rely on Travis Johnson and Salesi Moa moving forward. Whittingham noted that tight end Mason Bonner could also see some play. It's also concerning to see Rod Moore on the list after he played last weekend against Oregon. The Wolverines' secondary got beat a few times against Oregon, and having a veteran back there like Moore would only help against UCLA. away.headline: Kyle Whittingham updates Michigan injuries ahead of Ohio State game
away.blurb: While Marky Walbridge has improved week-over-week serving as the Wolverines' right tackle, Blake Frazier -- though better at left tackle -- would give Michigan that much better of an opportunity. While JJ Buchanan and Andrew Sprague are ruled out, getting Frazier back would be a big boost in the arm. There are two other players who very well could return -- another offensive lineman in Brady Norton, as well as running back Jordan Marshall, who has missed the past few games. Though the Wolverines have solid replacements at each of their positions, Whittingham would love to have both available. And at least one will be. “Brady Norton, we hope to get back this week,” Whittingham said. “He would have been available last week or on Saturday in an emergency situation. JJ, out for the year, like we said. Jordan Marshall. He hopefully will be back. It’s going to be close, but we’re hoping that we get him back this week.” “Jake Guarnera is a tough kid,” Whittingham said. “He has played through a lot of pain. Again, we’re not going to put a guy out there. Our trainers, our medical staff isn’t going to put anybody out there that is going to be in danger of furthering an injury. But he has been able to endure a lot of discomfort, and a lot of guys would not have been able to play with the discomfort that he’s been able to play with. So, credit to Jake. He’s a warrior.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- Michigan football has been shorthanded all year, and it'll hope to be closer to full strength on Saturday when it heads to Columbus to take on the most gettable version of Ohio State in more than a decade. The Wolverines and Buckeyes have four or more losses each entering The Game for the first time since 1966, and while there are questions about Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood, who was revealed as having an injury on Monday, there are certainly others the maize and blue would love to have back. Kyle Whittingham isn't sure whether he'll be able to go or not, but he does believe he's progressing. “He’s making progress, I can tell you that,” Whittingham said. “But we still do not have a definitive thumbs up or thumbs down for this week.” One player not spoken of as much is center Jake Guarnera, who has played through injury all year. He hasn't been so bad that he could make things worse, but he's battled through everything that's been thrown at him. Michigan and Ohio State are set to kick off at 12:10 p.m. EST at Ohio Stadium, with The Game set to air on Fox. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
away.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Michigan vs Ohio State is set for a noon kickoff on FOX.

Kyle Whittingham isn't sure whether he'll be able to go or not, but he does believe he's progressing. “He’s making progress, I can tell you that,” Whittingham said. “But we still do not have a definitive thumbs up or thumbs down for this week.” One player not spoken of as much is center Jake Guarnera, who has played through injury all year. He hasn't been so bad that he could make things worse, but he's battled through everything that's been thrown at him. Michigan and Ohio State are set to kick off at 12:10 p.m. EST at Ohio Stadium, with The Game set to air on Fox. home.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood dealing with injury heading into Ohio State game
home.blurb: At his press conference on Monday morning, Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham said that sophomore Bryce Underwood is set to start in The Game this weekend against Ohio State. However, we’ll see if he’s able to even play at all. Per 247Sports’ Matt Zenitz, Underwood is dealing with a lower-body injury that he suffered during Saturday’s stunning upset win over UCLA. His status is “in question” heading into The Game in Columbus this weekend. Underwood has had quite the roller coaster season. He started the first six games of the season before freshman Tommy Carr took over after halftime of the Penn State game. Carr was then benched two weeks ago during the game at Oregon, and Underwood has taken every snap since. Despite the injury, Whittingham told the media on Monday morning that Underwood is “the guy” at quarterback, and that “barring anything unforeseen, getting dinged up in practice or something like that,” he will start against the Buckeyes on Saturday. Underwood completed just 11-of-24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown on Saturday vs UCLA. He also ran 13 times for five yards, losing one fumble in the process. On the season, he has completed 85-of-156 passes (54.5 percent) for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions, while also running 76 times for 230 yards and an additional two scores. Should Underwood not be able to play in this one, Carr will be the next man up for the Wolverines. The true freshman has completed 67-of-106 passes this season for 686 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s also ran 49 times for 138 yards and three touchdowns. Michigan vs Ohio State is set for a noon kickoff on FOX.

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 25, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky hopes to snap a three-game losing streak and avoid losing a third straight game to Louisville. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. away.headline: Pat Kelsey delivers the Seth Trimble injury update Louisville needed ahead of Texas Tech
away.blurb: Last week in the Cardinals' sluggish win over Stetson, UofL was without their starting shooting guard, Seth Trimble. Leading up to the game, reports said Trimble would miss it with a “minor injury,” and they expected him to be available Tuesday for Louisville’s matchup with Texas Tech. After gaining eligibility through the “five-for-five rule,” Trimble was one of Kelsey’s biggest additions from the Transfer Portal. He has started in every game this year, except vs. Stetson, when he was out, and with Louisville looking to pull off the upset, the UNC transfer will have to be healthy. The good news is that Trimble sounds like he will play in this huge rank-vs-rank matchup, and he is trending toward a return. Pat Kelsey delivers the Seth Trimble injury update Louisville needed ahead of Texas Tech Skip to main content About Louisville basketball recruiting Thanksgiving week is here, which means Louisville basketball’s Players Era 16 run is about to start. The Cardinals are currently in Las Vegas, where they are scheduled to tip off Tuesday, Nov. 24, for their first matchup of the event. Pat Kelsey challenges Flory Bidunga to become a centerpiece of Louisville's offense The Cards will look to secure their first marquee win of the season, as they face No. 9 Texas Tech. UofL enters this matchup 3-1, including their recent 83-69 win over Stetson. Pat Kelsey has struggled against ranked teams in the past, and tomorrow’s matchup will be a big test for this Lousiville squad. On Sunday, the Cardinals held a virtual press conference ahead of their game against Texas Tech, and Louisville fans got the Seth Trimble injury update they wanted. Seth Trimble is expected to play Tuesday against Texas Tech On Sunday, Kelsey confirmed the report is still accurate, as the Cardinals' head coach expects the UNC transfer to play. "Seth, we expect him to play," stated Kelsey. The Cardinals will need Trimble on Tuesday to pull off this upset, as the UNC transfer is a key piece to Kelsey’s offense and defense. He is a physical guard who will defend the opposing team’s best guard and will force turnovers, as he is averaging 1.7 steals per game, including two steals in each of the past two games. In addition to his defense, he is an offensive threat, averaging 13.3 points per game, the third-highest on the team, behind Flory Bidunga and Adrian Wooley. Trimble spent his first four seasons at North Carolina, including last season, when he averaged 14.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. The Cardinals have just a 29% chance of winning, according to ESPN Analytics, as the Red Raiders enter this game 5-0. Texas Tech already has a marquee win this season after the Red Raiders defeated No. 3 Illinois 84-78. Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown (Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports - Clemson Tue, November 24, 2026 at 11:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Clemson Tigers were able to take down the Duke Blue Devils on the road last week, picking up a massive win for the season. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

Everything You Need to Know About the Clemson vs. South Carolina Odds COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Ryan Linthicum #53 of the Clemson Tigers prepares to snap the ball during the second half of a football game rolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Zach Lentz · HEAVY Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:52 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads CLEMSON, S.C. — The Palmetto Bowl returns to Death Valley on Saturday with pride, momentum, and a surprising betting line on the table. Despite boasting a better record and home-field advantage, the Clemson Tigers (7-4) are once again playing the underdog role. FanDuel oddsmakers have installed the South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5) as 5.5-point road favorites for the regular-season finale. The Gamecocks sit at -215 on the moneyline, while the Tigers offer +180 value. The over/under is set at a gritty 41.5 points. For the second consecutive year, both programs enter the rivalry unranked in the US LBM Coaches Poll, though Clemson quietly garnered 11 votes on Sunday. But national rankings rarely dictate the tempo of this bitter in-state clash. Clemson's Ground Game and Stifling Defense Clemson enters Saturday riding the high of a defensive masterclass. Just days ago, the Tigers walked into Durham as 13.5-point underdogs and dismantled Duke 20-10. The blueprint was simple: control the clock and suffocate the opposition. Clemson's defense allowed just 11 first downs all night, keeping the Blue Devils' offense on the field for a paltry 22 minutes and 45 seconds. By the time Duke regained possession following Chris Denson's 7-yard, fourth-quarter touchdown run, the game was effectively out of reach. Offensively, the Tigers unleashed a punishing, multi-pronged rushing attack. Three different players eclipsed the 50-yard mark, led by Jarvis Green's 84 yards on 16 carries and Denson's 71 yards. The catalyst, however, was Trent Pearman. In his first career start, the quarterback proved poised under pressure. Pearman completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards and added 51 yards on the ground. His decisive 9-yard touchdown scramble in the third quarter gave Clemson a lead it never relinquished. Now, he faces a South Carolina defense desperate for a bounce-back performance. Gamecocks Look to Rebound After Georgia Mauling South Carolina arrives in Death Valley needing a win to match Clemson's 7-4 record, but they must first shake off the lingering effects of a brutal 34-6 home loss to No. 1 Georgia. The Gamecocks' primary objective will be jumpstarting quarterback LaNorris Sellers. The top-ranked Bulldogs terrorized Sellers in the pocket, sacking him three times and intercepting him once. He finished the afternoon with just 87 passing yards and 24 rushing yards. If South Carolina is to cover the 5.5-point spread in one of college football's most hostile environments, Sellers will need the time and space that Georgia strictly denied him. Kickoff from Memorial Stadium is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET Saturday on ESPN2. Former Clemson football safety Khalil Barnes picks off South Carolina Drew Landon, Clemson Wire · Clemson Wire Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:24 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Khalil Barnes may have traded orange for red and black, but habits from longtime friends are hard to get rid of. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game. away.blurb: On one hand South Carolina looks like a difficult opponent since they've won four of their last five games, but they did lose to Arkansas 34-6 their last time out this past weekend. It'd be easy to think they are a team trending in the wrong direction now, but they didn't have star quarterback LaNorris Sellers during the Arkansas game. His status appears to be changing heading into Saturday's game though because he was not listed on South Carolina's official injury report on Wednesday night and it appears he will be available to play against Georgia this weekend. Georgia's injury report only had two names on it on Wednesday, and the one everyone will be closely watching is Drew Bobo. He is the Bulldogs starting center who missed his first game of the season last week against Missouri, and his status this week is still up in the air as he is questionable to play. At this point it seems unlikely that he will play, but even if he is out Georgia is still expected to beat South Carolina. All eyes will be on him though throughout the rest of this week, but if he still isn't 100 percent it might not be a bad idea to keep him on the sideline so he can get back to full health before Georgia's playoff run and the SEC Championship game. Georgia is just a few days away from their SEC finale . Their opponent, the South Carolina Gamecocks, are 6-4, winners of four of their last five games and the No. 21 team in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. South Carolina is a different beast with LaNorris Sellers Last weekend's loss to Arkansas was ugly. They are one of the worst teams in the SEC this season, so losing 34-6 to them is unacceptable with or without Sellers. That game likely would've gone much differently had Sellers played though, and it's easy to see that when looking at the four games they won in a row before this loss. During that four game win streak the Gamecocks had Sellers as their starting quarterback. Sellers led them to three wins over teams currently ranked as they beat Florida, Tennessee and Oklahoma along with a Texas A&M team who has underachieved this season but has loads of talent. Sellers specifically was dominant in these four games as he totaled nine touchdowns and threw for over 1,000 yards. South Carolina clearly missed him last week against Arkansas, but they could be in position to upset Georgia with him potentially coming back from injury this week. All eyes for Georgia are on Drew Bobo Backup center Cortez Smith played well in his place against Missouri, but Georgia is at their best with Bobo in the lineup. He has the most experience at the position by far and his connection with Gunner Stockton is one that no one else can replicate. away.headline: Major Update on Injury Report for South Carolina Gamecocks
away.blurb: Teams have released their first injury reports for the week. The most glaring omission from the report is the name of LaNorris Sellers . After being listed as questionable last week, Sellers was unable to participate against the Arkansas Razorbacks, which led to a blowout 34-6 loss. Sellers’s presence is a non-negotiable if the Gamecocks want to pull off an upset against the number one ranked Georgia Bulldogs , who arguably have the best defensive unit in the country. The Bulldogs have limited some of the best quarterbacks and offenses in the conference to a standstill, but Sellers could be one of the toughest tests they face all season. Though Sellers will be back, injury issues still loom over the Gamecocks. Leading rusher Matt Fuller IV is out. Receivers Mazeo Bennett Jr. and Nyck Harbor are listed as questionable along with EDGE’s Dylan Stewart and Anthony Addison. DB Judge Collier is also listed as questionable. Unfortunately, the South Carolina Gamecocks are no exception. However, it seems their most pressing injury concern may have been resolved. Sellers sustained an ankle early in the win over the Texas A&M Aggies. Despite the injury, the Florence, SC native dashed past the Aggie defense for a 41-yard touchdown rush that was ultimately the dagger and sealed the win. The score was especially impressive given his injury, as he ended up leaving the field hopping on one foot, as his ankle was too sore to put any pressure on. away.headline: South Carolina vs. Georgia: Kickoff time, TV channel, injury report, odds
away.blurb: WR Nitro Tuggle, DB Jalewis Soloman, WR Jayden Sellers, RB Matt Fuller, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. WR Mazeo Bennett, EDGE Dylan Stewart, DB Judge Collier, WR Nyck Harbor and EDGE Anthony Addison are all listed as questionable. All five of those players are starters at their respective positions and would be a massive loss should they not play this weekend. What’s going on at QB? There was confusion galore around South Carolina’s quarterback room last week. Is LaNorris Sellers healthy? Would he be available? Is he going to play? What’s the definition of probable? Does anything anyone says really mean anything? The answer to those questions was that Cutter Woods started at quarterback for South Carolina in its loss to Arkansas. USC offensive coordinator Kendal Briles said “all” of the Gamecock quarterbacks practiced on Wednesday. It remains to be seen if Sellers will return from the ankle injury he sustained vs. Texas A&M or if Woods will get the second start of his career. Is all CFP hope lost? South Carolina’s hopes of making the College Football Playoff seemed completely lost after it was upset on the road by Arkansas last week. After all, there’s no way a team with four losses who was just defeated by an unranked team would stick around in the CFP rankings…right? Wrong. South Carolina remained in the CFP Top 25 , only dropping from No. 17 to No. 21. The odds of making the playoff are very slim but should South Carolina find a way to win out by beating No. 1 Georgia and Clemson then there’s a world where its playoff odds may graduate to just slim . Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks will face No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. The game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. and be televised nationally on ABC. South Carolina (6-4, 4-4 SEC) is coming off a loss to Arkansas last week. Meanwhile, Georgia (9-1, 7-1 SEC) is coming off a win over Missouri at home. Georgia leads the all-time series over South Carolina 55-19-2. The Bulldogs have won the last four games in the series, including the last matchup in 2023. South Carolina’s last win in the series came in upset fashion in 2019. The Gamecocks haven’t beat Georgia at home in Columbia since 2014. Here’s everything you need to know about Saturday’s game. home.blurb: Star cornerback Elliot Washington II, tied for second nationally with five interceptions, is now a game-time decision after being questionable. Branden Strozier was taking first-team reps at outside cornerback, while Marcell Gipson Jr. was taking first-team reps at nickel. Wide receiver Tyler Brown, right guard Easton Ware, defensive tackle Champ Thompson and linebacker Jeremiah Alexander are all out. Alexander has made 56 total tackles this season. C.J. Kubah-Taylor and Fletcher Cothran are among the linebackers who could see more playing time with Alexander out. Kobe McCloud can too, as he has been removed from the report after missing the Syracuse game on Nov. 7 and returning against Georgia Tech on Nov. 14. Elyjah Thurmon on track to return New additions to Clemson's report also include quarterbacks Tait Reynolds (knee) and Christopher Vizzina (concussion). Reynolds is out for the season with a meniscus tear in his left knee , and Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said he doesn't have a timeline for Vizzina's return, who he said suffered a "severe" concussion against Georgia Tech. Defensive tackles Champ Thompson and Vic Burley are also new additions. Thompson's injury is unknown and will keep him out of the Duke game, while Swinney said Burley (foot) will need surgery and will be out for the season. Defensive end Kevin O'Connor (Duke's sack leader with five) and Bryce Davis, and cornerback Dylan Flowers and Kyon Loud have all been removed after being originally listed as probable. CB Elliot Washington II (game-time decision) Clemson football starting center Harris Sewell and running back Gideon Davidson have both been removed from the availability report for the Duke game, putting them on track to play. However, Sewell was seen taking second-team reps behind freshman Grant Wise. The Tigers (6-4, 4-3 ACC) face the Blue Devils (7-3, 4-3) in a road game on Nov. 20 (7:30 p.m., ESPN).
