Because of this, Clemson will need a few pieces to step up to slow down Duke this weekend. Fourth-year wideout Tyler Brown was just announced to be out of Friday’s contest, and Preston is the next man up on the depth chart to play with the likes of Bryant Wesco Jr. and T.J. Moore against Duke. He was able to flash the potential in last week’s loss as well. Preston finished with four catches for 56 yards in the loss, leading the team in both of those categories as well as breaking a 33-yard catch in the contest. The Alexandria, Virginia, native has had to wait behind that starting trio throughout the entire season, but Friday is another opportunity to show why he was a four-star recruit coming out of high school. The season-ending injuries to both Donovan Starr and Corian Gipson have given the true freshman a chance to compete early in his Clemson career. With Elliot Washington II being a game-time decision until the game on Friday, Gipson’s role could be even heightened against the Blue Devils. The Dallas native saw elevated time last weekend and recorded a tackle in the loss, continuing to grow in his first season of college football. He sits behind senior Branden Strozier in the depth chart at the TIGER position, but if Washington can’t go, Strozier would be bumped out wide, leaving the freshman in the versatile spot on defense. Thursday night’s injury report saw starter Jeremiah Alexander downgraded to out for the matchup with Duke. Behind him in the depth chart is Cothran, a former walk-on, who will look to finish his senior season strong against a tough Duke front. picks.blurb: Week 13 College Football Predictions: College Football Picks for Rivalry Week, including USC vs UCLA Opens in a new tab Sportsnaut NFL NFL Schedule NFL Standings NFL Power Rankings NFL Defense Rankings NFL Offense Rankings NFL QB Rankings MLB MLB Power Rankings MLB Standings NBA NBA Playoffs Bracket NBA Power Rankings 50 Best NBA Players NHL NHL Standings NHL Power Rankings NASCAR NASCAR Standings NASCAR Power Rankings UFC Men's Pound for Pound Rankings Women's Pound for Pound Rankings COLLEGE College Basketball College Football Other College Sports High School Sports Add Sportsnaut on Google Add on Google Facebook The 2026 college football regular season draws to a close this weekend with Rivalry Week. Much of the chaos and surprises from throughout the fall have slightly diminished some of the matchups for things like The Game and the Egg Bowl, but it’s still worth making college football picks this weekend for a slate of games that mean so much to these programs. Let’s dive into our Week 13 college football picks this weekend for the top rivalry matchups. Ole Miss Rebels 38, Mississippi State Bulldogs 17 The Ole Miss Rebels are out of College Football Playoff contention, and the Mississippi State Bulldogs have been in a free fall since the 4-0 start to the season. While there aren’t major stakes for the Egg Bowl, this in-state battle still features two teams and fan bases that very much hate one another. Unfortunately for the Bulldogs, this offense hasn’t been the same since Kamario Taylor’s season-ending injury. In the last five games against SEC opponents, Mississippi State is averaging just 10 PPG with single-digit points against LSU, Texas and Auburn. Defensively, things have been nearly just as bad. In what could be his final start as the Rebels’ quarterback, Trinidad Chambliss will clear 300 total yards with four touchdowns and win the Egg Bowl for the second consecutive year. Iowa Hawkeyes 20, Nebraska Cornhuskers 14 The Iowa Hawkeyes steamrolled through the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Black Friday last season, with Kamari Moulton and Mark Gronowski combining for four rushing touchdowns and taking full advantage of their rival having no semblance of a passing game. Fast forward to 2026, Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule now has a viable threat in Anthony Colandrea, with his big-play ability proving instrumental in the win last week at Ohio State. Here’s the issue for Nebraska. Iowa boasts the second-best red zone defense (67.9% scoring rate) in the nation this season, and it ranks 11th among Power Four defenses in yards per play allowed (4.6). The Cornhuskers offense is inconsistent, as evidenced by a four-game stretch from Oct. 10 through Nov. 6 when it averaged just 13.5 PPG. This will be a much closer game than what took place last year, but the Hawkeyes’ defense and run game will pave the way to a win at home. Texas Longhorns 21, Texas A&M Aggies 7 Arch Manning is coming off one of his sharpest performances of the season, and he’s completed at least 73% of his passes with three-plus total touchdowns in three of his last four games. He does, however, still have a penchant for making poor decisions under pressure, and Mike Elko’s defense can get after the quarterback. Unfortunately for the Texas A&M Aggies, they have one of the worst offenses in the Power Four. This is a matchup ripe with opportunities for the Texas Longhorns defense to record four-plus sacks and multiple takeaways, regardless of who the Aggies’ starting quarterback in Week 13 is. As long as Manning doesn’t turn it over three times, Texas will win this one comfortably at Kyle Field. Ohio State Buckeyes 13, Michigan Wolverines 10 Neither the Ohio State Buckeyes nor the Michigan Wolverines are ranked entering The Game, a scenario that seemed unfathomable before the season kicked off. Michigan’s defense has been one of its few bright spots this season, and it should be able to take advantage of a leaky Buckeyes offensive line, limiting how many opportunities Luke Fahey has to target Jeremiah Smith downfield. The Wolverines also have some momentum coming into this one, with freshman running back Savion Hiter (108 scrimmage yards) and edge rusher John Henry Daley (two sacks) having just led them to an upset win over UCLA. However, Ohio State’s lone strength defensively this season has been its ability to stop the run (3.2 ypc and 100.3 rushing yards per game allowed). This is going to be an ugly football game, and there’s a path to Michigan embarrassing Ryan Day at home if Bryce Underwood can take advantage of facing an ineffective Buckeyes pass rush or the Wolverines let him and Hiter run wild with the RPO. Ohio State is favored here, and both teams figure to rely heavily on the run game. Ultimately, we think both the home-field advantage and the very different tone being set for The Game by both coaches leads to the Buckeyes pulling out an ugly one. Plus, one team has Smith and the other doesn’t. Louisville Cardinals 27, Kentucky Wildcats 24 The Louisville Cardinals and Kentucky Wildcats find themselves in two very different places coming into Week 13. Kentucky was in the top 10 of the College Football Playoff Rankings back in the first week of November, and it’s now lost three consecutive games, with two of those by double digits. Meanwhile, Louisville has clawed its way back from a 2-3 record after losing at NC State with a six-game winning streak, albeit those wins have come against some very bad competition. One thing we’re keeping an eye on: the Wildcats defense has allowed the ninth-highest passer rating (174.4) and yards per attempt ( 9.5 ) in college football over the last three weeks. Meanwhile, Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz is coming off a five-touchdown performance, and this is a chance for him to potentially boost his stock further before shopping himself around to quarterback-needy programs this offseason. We just see a Kentucky program that is spiraling out of control under first-year head coach Will Stein, and there’s a lack of confidence in him salvaging it against Jeff Brohm’s Cardinals. Momentum, head-coaching experience and the better quarterback allow Louisville to win on the road. USC Trojans 20, UCLA Bruins 13 The UCLA Bruins aren’t ruling out quarterback Ty Dieffenbach playing on Saturday against the USC Trojans. We’re just not buying it and tend to believe it’s a bit of gamesmanship by head coach Bob Chesney. That would mean the Bruins are forced into starting Madden Iamaleava, who looked like one of the worst quarterbacks in college football coming in for relief against Michigan. UCLA still has a chance in this one because its defense has been spectacular throughout the season, allowing the lowest yards-per-play average (4.0), the sixth-lowest conversion rate on third down (29.22%) and the seventh-fewest red zone opportunities per game (2.5). With that said, running back Wayne Knight’s performance has plummeted in recent weeks. Against Wisconsin, Michigan State, Nevada, Illinois and Michigan, he totaled just 218 rushing yards (43.6 per game) and averaged only 3.2 yards per carry. While UCLA has the better head coach, its issues at quarterback and the sudden inability to run the football as effectively as they did earlier in the season will be its downfall against Lincoln Riley and Jayden Maiava. Oregon Ducks 34, Washington Huskies 24 Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola is on a hot streak right now, coming into this game with 1,168 passing yards (292 pass ypg), a 10-0 TD-INT line and a 66.2% completion rate in the last four games. We are not, however, buying into this two-game stretch from the Ducks defense and firmly believe this side of the ball is what opens the door to the Washington Huskies potentially pulling off the upset on Saturday night. With this game being played in Eugene and Dan Lanning’s program having a shot to earn a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, we do think the Ducks will come out highly motivated for this one and deliver their fourth consecutive win by double-digit points. Alabama Crimson Tide 28, Auburn Tigers 14 We can’t wait to see how the College Football Playoff committee turns this into another incredible victory for the Alabama Crimson Tide. The Auburn Tigers did win at Georgia back on Oct. 17, with quarterback Byrum Brown torching them on the ground for 115 yards. Brown has also done a much better job of protecting the football in the second half of the season, throwing just one interception on 149 pass attempts after having seven picks in his first five games. Alabama’s defense is, however, very good at both creating takeaways and forcing athletic quarterbacks to beat them from the pocket. The Crimson Tide will generate two takeaways in the Iron Bowl, and a three-touchdown performance by Keelon Russell will propel this team to victory. Got a story or tip for us? picks.headline: USC Trojans vs UCLA Bruins Prediction | Nov. 28, 2026
Rivalry game predictions: UCLA football vs. USC
picks.blurb: Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026 Sports Columns The 2023 UCLA football team celebrates around the Victory Bell. The Bruins' last win over the Trojans was three years ago. (Daily Bruin file photo) By Jacob Nguyen , Kai Dizon , Alexandra Crosnoe , Lucine Ekizian , and Nora Gallagher Nov. 22, 2026 8:07 p.m. This post was updated Nov. 22 at 8:26 p.m. No. 4 UCLA football (10-1, 7-1 Big Ten) closes out its 2026 season in its annual crosstown showdown against rival No. 18 USC (8-3, 5-3) Saturday at the Rose Bowl. Having lost the previous two rivalry matchups, the Bruins have an opportunity to punch their ticket to the Big Ten championship game on Dec. 5. Here are the final regular-season game predictions from Sports editor Jacob Nguyen and Sports senior staffer Kai Dizon, along with guest predictions from editor-in-chief Alexandra Crosnoe, managing editor Lucine Ekizian and digital managing editor Nora Gallagher. Jacob Nguyen Sports editor Prediction: UCLA 7, USC 28 I’m honestly getting emotional writing this. It’s been an amazing ride covering the Bruins this year, being able to watch a historic turnaround and make predictions for UCLA victories week in and week out. While I missed getting a couple of these renditions posted, I entered every matchup with the prediction – whether verbalized online or not – that the Bruins would come out on top. I said so to open the season against California. I hesitantly said so against then-No. 13 Oregon on the road. And I said so again even when senior quarterback Nico Iamaleava was sidelined with an injury. As the season went on, my belief in this program slowly morphed from delusion into genuine confidence, as the Bruins continued finding ways to win. As much as it hurts to see UCLA fall short of a program-best 11-0 record, knowing that it took triple overtime, a two-point conversion and another injury at signal-caller to defeat the Bruins says a lot about this squad. To put it bluntly, I’m not confident UCLA maintains any semblance of its offensive cohesion with sophomore quarterback Madden Iamaleava. I had more fiery things to say about all that in a separate column, so I’ll be conservative with my words here. All I’ll say is that – should I be proven wrong – it will be because of UCLA’s defense, which is one of the strongest units in the entire country. But the margin of error with Iamaleava under center feels even less than paper-thin. At the very least, I can be happy that the Rose Bowl should be bustling, with its tarps being removed since being introduced in 2021. No matter what happens, I’m just thankful I got to see this team all year. I truly love this job. And I’m not just saying that because I’m sharing bylines with my bosses. Kai Dizon Daily Bruin senior staff Prediction: UCLA 22, USC 21 Bruin fans should thank Madden Iamaleava – he’s given UCLA a scapegoat. The sophomore quarterback will shield senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach from ridicule over his one-interception, four-fumble, 188-yard performance. He’ll make people forget senior cornerback Scooter Jackson had a game-winning interception slip right between his hands. Because Iamaleava forgot how to run, fewer people are going to blame the Bruins’ running back Cerberus, which lost all of its bite against Michigan – with fifth-year Wayne Knight accumulating just 30 yards on 11 carries, fifth-year Anthony Woods racking up just 14 yards on four carries, and senior Jaivian Thomas 30 yards on five carries. Iamaleava – who has a 33% completion rate in his collegiate career and started just a single year in high school – will make it all the more easy to forget a banged-up Bruin defense let freshman running back Savion Hiter pick up over 100 yards on the ground. UCLA did not lose to Michigan because of one player – but it sure did look that way. If the Bruins are any good, Saturday’s loss rang their bell at just the right time. The only thing more important than staying up is being able to get back up once you fall. And Iamaleava’s sacrifice means his locker room can all point their fingers toward him, rather than at each other, while the outside noise screams at him and not his teammates, granting the rest of the Bruins some much-needed silence. Rest now, brother – we’ll see you in Valhalla. Alexandra Crosnoe Editor in chief Prediction: UCLA 13, USC 10 There are certain moments in college football that are hard to come by and hard to forget. For Bruin fans, one of those moments might’ve come during UCLA’s Nov. 13 matchup against Illinois. Pelting rain had slowed to a hazy drizzle, muddying the view of the field. And out of the murk emerged Dieffenbach, the improbable second-string phenom who’d, to that point, kept the Bruins’ perfect season alive for four games after injury sidelined their starter. A hard hit kept Dieffenbach out for nearly the entire third quarter, and Bruin fans had certainly seen enough of third-string Iamaleava in that time. The Rose Bowl hummed. After a quarter of fretting over what would become of the Bruins’ season-saving grace – and reckoning with the biting reminder that UCLA has a history of faltering when it means the most – Dieffenbach’s return solidified a belief that brought nearly every fan to their feet: This season isn’t a fluke. What happened at the Big House on Saturday, then, felt like a cruel inversion of that awe-inspiring Rose Bowl episode. After a Wolverine defender brought Dieffenbach down clean on his knee, a cart hauled him off the field and Iamaleava suited up, it quickly became clear that nobody – and certainly not the third-stringer – could save UCLA from conceding its unblemished record. There’s no disputing that without Dieffenbach, what once seemed like a surefire bid to the postseason is certainly in limbo. But I haven’t seen enough to let that moment against Illinois slip away. All season, UCLA has continued to find a way, and a combination of faith in the Bruins’ elite coaching staff, creative play-calling and, of course, blind buy-in tells me it’ll do the same with its season on the line. With a competent signal-caller – possibly in sophomore Colton Gumino or freshman DJ Bordeaux – some wildcat action, and the talent that carried the Bruins to their school’s greatest single-season turnaround all year long, UCLA can eke out a low-scoring victory. Dieffenbach might not be coming back. But the Bruins, who went 3-9 last season, are no strangers to beating the odds. Knowing at the start of the season that UCLA could make the playoffs would've left both the pundits and patrons dumbfounded. I’m ready to bet on the people who believed it might happen all along . Mark my words: come Saturday, we’ll see the Bruins haul the victory bell back to Westwood. Lucine Ekizian Managing editor Prediction: UCLA 10, USC 7 Following Dieffenbach's injury, UCLA football resorted to its third-string quarterback against Michigan on Saturday. This closely followed the Bruins watching an undefeated season slip through their fingers. Two injured quarterbacks and a snapped win streak could be enough to break UCLA’s morale ahead of its USC matchup. But UCLA isn’t a program defined by its losses. The Bruins ended their 2025 season with an unremarkable record of 3-9. Now, with coach Bob Chesney at the helm, they stand at No. 4 – the highest College Football Playoff ranking in school history. Saturday’s loss doesn’t seal the Bruins’ trajectory, nor does it come close to wiping away the team’s 10 wins thus far. It took triple overtime for the Bruins to be handed their first upset of the season. Even with the loss, UCLA limited Michigan to 120 rushing yards and has a No. 3-ranked defense that will prove to be a barrier for its crosstown rivals. In big games, USC fails to skillfully execute its defense – giving up 3.58 points per drive across its losses against then-No. 20 Oregon, Wisconsin and then-No. 9 Indiana. And, if there’s anyone who can remind UCLA of its Chesney-era triumphs and further shake up USC’s defense, it's the Bruin faithful at the Rose Bowl. Despite rain and wind, attendance for a UCLA football game at the Rose Bowl reached its season peak when the Bruins took down the Fighting Illini on Nov. 13. For the Nov. 28 crosstown matchup, the tarps that have covered the seats on the north side of the Rose Bowl since 2021 are coming down – UCLA is preparing for an energetic Bruin crowd. The shock will wear off from UCLA’s win streak getting busted. It’ll result in an 11-1 record. Nora Gallagher Digital managing editor Prediction: UCLA 7, USC 20 As Dieffenbach exited the Big House on a stretcher Saturday evening, UCLA’s shot at a win over USC left with him. Make no mistake: I was optimistic UCLA could best Michigan. Through the shaky second half, through the nail-biting 10-10 tie and even through the celebrated quarterback’s startling first-overtime injury, I held out hope. Then I watched Iamaleava play. The third-string quarterback’s floundering performance in triple overtime deflated my glass-half-full attitude within seconds of his taking over the gridiron. I am hardly a football savant – and Iamaleava was undoubtedly handed a difficult task – but even I know the Long Beach local sacrificed wide-open lanes and squandered critical passes. As the Wolverine faithful cheered their men to a devastating 18-16 defeat over UCLA, the sobering truth emerged: Chesney’s historic run with this Westwood squad is through. Even before the fateful Dieffenbach-Iamaleava swap, though, there were signs that the Bruins may have maxed out their potential. Going touchdown-less for nearly the first 60 minutes of the game, UCLA routinely turned over the ball and faltered defensively. Though I will Fight Off from dawn to dusk at the Rose Bowl on Saturday, I will know – as I suspect many Bruin fans will – that UCLA, devoid of Dieffenbach, is destined to lose.

away.blurb: The USC Trojans are coming into their matchup against the Tarleton State Texans on Thursday evening looking to add to their four-game win streak to begin the 2026-27 college basketball season. However, the team is going to be short-handed. Both Onyeka Joe Agu and Eric Reibe were ruled out for USC due to injury, as per Jon Rothstein of 247Sports.com USC gets 2 unfortunate injury updates for Tarleton State clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB USC gets 2 unfortunate injury updates for Tarleton State clash David Yapkowitz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Onyeka Joe Agu is nursing a groin injury while Eric Reibe is dealing with a foot injury for USC's game against Tarleton State. Neither player has suited up for the Trojans yet this season. Agu is a freshman whole Reibe is a sophomore. Reibe transferred to USC via the portal after spending his freshman season at UConn. The young big man appeared in 40 games for the Huskies, including five starts, at a little over 13 minutes per game. He averaged 5.9 points and 3.3 rebounds with splits of 65.8 percent shooting from the field, 30.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 52.1 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 20-year-old suffered the injury during the offseason , a re-aggravation of a previous injury, and is in the rehab process following surgery. Reibe was expected to play a key role for the Trojans this season as he continues his development. With Joe Agu, the amount of playing time and role he would have had with USC this season was a little less certain. He was part of a heralded recruiting class for the Trojans that included five-star twin centers Darius and Adonis Ratliff, and five-star forward Christian Collins. Joe Agu joined the team after beginning his basketball career in his home country of Belgium. He most recently played in the BNXT league, a joint basketball venture between Belgium and the Netherlands. home.blurb: The report matters past this week. Thamel said Dieffenbach should be available for the College Football Playoff if UCLA earns a berth. Whether its quarterback can face USC is an open question. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Monday that Dieffenbach has a minor hip injury and should avoid a lengthy absence. His status for Saturday's rivalry game is iffy. Thus, the Bruins have a decent outlook following a painful trip to Michigan. They lost their quarterback in overtime and suffered their first defeat, 18-16, in three extra periods. UCLA fell to 10-1 overall and 7-1 in Big Ten play. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) Dieffenbach went down on a 6-yard run during UCLA's first overtime possession Saturday. Medical personnel placed him on a stretcher and carted him from the field. Monday's report offers a less severe outlook than that scene suggested. He took four sacks, according to the official box score . Madden Iamaleava replaced him. The reserve missed his only pass attempt and finished with minus-1 rushing yard on two carries. UCLA settled for field goals in the first two overtimes, then failed on its two-point attempt in the third. Michigan converted its ensuing try to end the game. The Bruins had forced overtime with 10 seconds left in regulation. Running back Anthony Woods threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to tight end Brayden Loftin. home.blurb: So in other words, Chesney and UCLA aren't ruling him out for Saturday. That means USC and coach Lincoln Riley will have to prepare for multiple quarterbacks from what it appears. Reyna, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Mon, November 23, 2026 at 10:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads UCLA football woke up Monday realizing quarterback Ty Dieffenbach won't miss the remainder of the season . But will coach Bob Chesney and the Bruins have him ready for USC? Even after getting carted off against Michigan? Chesney offered an inspiring update on that front Monday. "It's a little bit better than we thought," Chesney shared with reporters. "We got X-rays right there on the spot, and those were clean. He's nowhere near in the clear, but at the same point in time, he's going to do everything in his power to get himself ready for USC." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Signs still indicate that Madden Iamaleava will start, though, amid Dieffenbach's health scare. Iamaleava will need to redeem himself after struggling in Ann Arbor this past Saturday. Chesney says Iamaleava is attacking his preparation differently . "Madden after the game was in a spot where he didn't love the way it was. But he's already back here and already had two different meetings with Coach [Dean] Kennedy, and just continues to find ways to get better and and do what he's got to do," Chesney said. Bragging rights in Los Angeles aren't the only thing on the minds of the Bruins this week. Same with clinching a Big Ten Conference title game berth. And also solidifying a College Football Playoff spot. Michigan's upset of UCLA threw the Bruins' pursuit of both in chaos. Now the Big Ten title game could see an Oregon versus Iowa showdown if UCLA loses. The Sooners have won three straight games since being embarrassed by South Carolina on Halloween at home. OU is 3-0 and has defeated Florida, Ole Miss and Texas A&M since firing Ben Arbuckle and promoting Jason Witten to interim offensive coordinator. With the way Witten has transformed OU's offense the past few weeks, it's becoming increasingly likely coach Brent Venables will remove the interim tag. The Sooners and Tigers will kick at 3:15 p.m. at Faurot Field in Columbia. The two programs have met 98 times with OU winning 68 of those matchups. Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

Copy Link copied Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables discusses the challenges Missouri presents on both sides of the ball as the Sooners prepare for their regular-season finale in Columbia. Oklahoma will look to extend its winning streak to four games and finish the regular season with eight wins when the Sooners travel to Missouri on Saturday. Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables said Tuesday that the Tigers present a significant challenge on both sides of the ball, particularly given their ability to protect the football and their success at home this season. Missouri is 5-1 at home and leads the SEC in turnover margin. Venables praised Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons for his decision-making and efficiency, noting that Simmons has thrown for more than 2,500 yards with just four interceptions this season. The Tigers also feature running back Jamal Roberts, who has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards this season, and a receiving corps that has helped Missouri become more explosive offensively. Venables said limiting big plays, tackling well and maintaining discipline will be important for Oklahoma’s defense against Missouri’s balanced offense. He also credited Missouri’s defensive front and the team’s fundamentals under head coach Eli Drinkwitz. “This is a team that’s gonna force you to play very clean fundamentally,” Venables said. The Sooners (7-4, 5-3 SEC) enter Saturday’s matchup having won three consecutive games, including a 28-7 victory over Texas A&M in their final home game of the season. Oklahoma’s offensive improvement during that stretch has come under interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten. Venables praised Witten’s work but declined to provide a timeline for naming a permanent offensive coordinator. “Jason’s done a fantastic job. That goes without saying,” Venables said. “You guys will find out soon enough.” Venables said Witten has provided clear direction for the offensive coaching staff and helped establish expectations following the midseason change. He also credited improved health, offensive balance and the team’s ability to sustain drives for its recent success. Quarterback John Mateer has played a significant role in Oklahoma’s late-season turnaround, accounting for all four touchdowns in Saturday’s victory over Texas A&M. Venables praised Mateer’s response to criticism and setbacks throughout his time at Oklahoma, pointing to his maturity and willingness to take responsibility. “He’s hung in there, and he’s made the best of it, and I’m proud of him,” Venables said. Looking ahead to next season, Venables said quarterbacks Whit Newbauer and Bo Bentley have benefited from additional practice repetitions while the coaching staff has managed Mateer’s workload. He said there is an opportunity for either young quarterback to compete for the starting job next season. With early signing day approaching, Venables also expressed optimism about Oklahoma’s player retention efforts, saying several players have indicated they intend to return next season. He said the Sooners have a promising foundation along the offensive line, with six high school players expected to join the program and additional opportunities to address depth through the transfer portal. As Oklahoma prepares for its final regular-season game, Venables said he is thankful for the way his players have continued to respond throughout the season. The Sooners will travel to Columbia on Saturday looking to carry their late-season momentum into the postseason. Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables discusses the challenges Missouri presents on both sides of the ball as the Sooners prepare for their regular-season finale in Columbia. Oklahoma will look to extend its winning streak to four games and finish the regular season with eight wins when the Sooners travel to Missouri on Saturday. Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables said Tuesday that the Tigers present a significant challenge on both sides of the ball, particularly given their ability to protect the football and their success at home this season. Missouri is 5-1 at home and leads the SEC in turnover margin. Venables praised Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons for his decision-making and efficiency, noting that Simmons has thrown for more than 2,500 yards with just four interceptions this season. The Tigers also feature running back Jamal Roberts, who has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards this season, and a receiving corps that has helped Missouri become more explosive offensively. Venables said limiting big plays, tackling well and maintaining discipline will be important for Oklahoma’s defense against Missouri’s balanced offense. He also credited Missouri’s defensive front and the team’s fundamentals under head coach Eli Drinkwitz. “This is a team that’s gonna force you to play very clean fundamentally,” Venables said. The Sooners (7-4, 5-3 SEC) enter Saturday’s matchup having won three consecutive games, including a 28-7 victory over Texas A&M in their final home game of the season. Oklahoma’s offensive improvement during that stretch has come under interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten. Venables praised Witten’s work but declined to provide a timeline for naming a permanent offensive coordinator. “Jason’s done a fantastic job. That goes without saying,” Venables said. “You guys will find out soon enough.” Venables said Witten has provided clear direction for the offensive coaching staff and helped establish expectations following the midseason change. He also credited improved health, offensive balance and the team’s ability to sustain drives for its recent success. Quarterback John Mateer has played a significant role in Oklahoma’s late-season turnaround, accounting for all four touchdowns in Saturday’s victory over Texas A&M. Venables praised Mateer’s response to criticism and setbacks throughout his time at Oklahoma, pointing to his maturity and willingness to take responsibility. “He’s hung in there, and he’s made the best of it, and I’m proud of him,” Venables said. Looking ahead to next season, Venables said quarterbacks Whit Newbauer and Bo Bentley have benefited from additional practice repetitions while the coaching staff has managed Mateer’s workload. He said there is an opportunity for either young quarterback to compete for the starting job next season. With early signing day approaching, Venables also expressed optimism about Oklahoma’s player retention efforts, saying several players have indicated they intend to return next season. He said the Sooners have a promising foundation along the offensive line, with six high school players expected to join the program and additional opportunities to address depth through the transfer portal. As Oklahoma prepares for its final regular-season game, Venables said he is thankful for the way his players have continued to respond throughout the season. The Sooners will travel to Columbia on Saturday looking to carry their late-season momentum into the postseason. Drake Johnson Drake Johnson is a Digital Sports Reporter for Griffin Media, covering Oklahoma sports for News On 6 and News 9. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. CB Dezz Ricks: game-time decision Everything seems to be going right for the Oklahoma Sooners right now, including a shrinking injury report. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. Washington's win over Indiana on Saturday gave the Ducks control of their own destiny in the Big Ten Championship Game, and now the table is set. If Oregon wins, the Ducks are into the Big Ten Championship Game, and a win in Indianapolis ensures a bid into the College Football Playoff this season. Dan Lanning's team has a clear path to the playoff now, and the first obstacle is a Huskies squad that just showed they're capable of pulling off big upsets. away.blurb: A total of eight players appeared on Indiana's Week 12 availability report on Thursday night. Six of those players have already been ruled out for Saturday's contest against the Huskies, and that group includes some key starters. The biggest losses for Indiana come on the offensive side of the ball. RB Turbo Richard and OL Joe Brunner both being unavailable for the second straight week is a tough blow to Indiana's rushing attack. After taking down USC by a score of 27-13 last week, the Indiana Hoosiers are hitting the road in Week 12. Traveling across the country to Seattle, this weekend's tilt against Washington is the furthest road trip of the regular season for IU. For the most part, Indiana has stayed relatively healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has a solid strategy in place to keep his players healthy, which includes prioritizing player recovery, managing practice workloads, and ensuring athletes receive proper rest and conditioning throughout the season. But at the end of the day, this is still football and injuries happen. Heading into Week 12, the Hoosiers are dealing with some injuries to key players that present some challenges against Washington. Indiana Football Week 12 injury report Here's a look at the full availability report for Indiana heading into Week 12: Richard was brought in from Boston College over the offseason to be Indiana's RB1, and he thrived in that role when healthy. Richard has rushed for 745 yards and team-leading 6.6 yards per carry with 6 touchdowns this season. The good news is that Khobie Martin is back after missing the first half of the season with a broken forearm, and he rushed 12 times for 82 yards and a touchdown last week against USC. Lee Beebe Jr. has also been a reliable rushing force this season, and he totaled 71 yards on 16 carries last week against the Trojans. With Richard sidelined, Martin and Beebe figure to share the workload in the Hoosier backfield once again. Brunner is a fifth-year senior who has been a key part of Indiana's offensive line this season. He transferred to Indiana from Wisconsin back in the spring, and brought plenty of experience with him as he appeared in 39 games with 24 starts during his career with the Badgers. Owning a 6'7" 320-pound frame, Brunner started the first nine games of the season at right guard for the Hoosiers. In his absence, redshirt sophomore Austin Liebfried got the starting nod at right guard against USC on Saturday afternoon. He could be expected to continue in that role, but freshman Sam Simpson could also see expanded opportunities. Last week without Richard and Brunner, Indiana ran for 146 yards and 4.2 yards per carry against USC. Washington's run defense isn't the best in the world, as the Huskies rank 10th in the Big Ten by allowing 132.4 rushing yards per game to their opponents. home.headline: Michigan State Receives Brutal Injury News Ahead of Senior Night vs. Oregon
home.blurb: Milivojevic is one of 10 Spartans listed out on the Big Ten availability report, with seven more listed questionable, according to Connor Earegood of The Detroit News . It is the second game Milivojevic has missed this season. Backup Cam Fancher is listed as questionable with a knee injury. If Fancher cannot go, true freshman Kayd Coffman is in line for the start. Coffman has already made a start this season and has completed 4 of 11 passes for 42 yards with one touchdown and one interception, per ESPN's team statistics . Who else is out for the Spartans on Senior Night Beyond Milivojevic, Michigan State lists defensive tackle Ben Roberts, safety Devin Vaught, linebacker Jordan Hall, running back Marvis Parrish, tight end Jayden Savoury, running back Cam Edwards, fullback Jay Coyne, offensive lineman Tristan Comer and tight end Joe Caudill as out, per Chris Solari of the Detroit Free Press . Alongside Fancher, the questionable list carries left guard Conner Moore, tight end Brennan Parachek, safety Michael Richard, running back Jaziun Patterson, receiver Rodney Bullard Jr. and cornerback Tre Bell. That is a thin roster for a team that has already been eliminated from bowl contention and is playing for its seniors. Dante Moore, the Detroit King product who opened the season as Oregon's starter, has not played since September and is out again on Friday. Ducks coach Dan Lanning said this week that he does not anticipate Moore playing again this season, according to Athlon Sports . Dylan Raiola has carried the offense since, completing 141 of 213 passes for 1,695 yards with 15 touchdowns and two interceptions, per ESPN . Oregon lists nine players out in all: Moore, running back Jordon Davison, receiver Iverson Hooks, defensive back Aaron Flowers, inside linebacker Brayden Platt, outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti, defensive lineman Matthew Johnson and offensive linemen Trent Ferguson and Dave Iuli. Inside linebacker Jerry Mixon is doubtful and defensive lineman Bear Alexander is probable, per Sports Illustrated's Oregon site , which reported Hooks was the one addition to the list. home.blurb: Oregon already needed to lean more on Smith in the last three games with running back Jordon Davison out due to injury. Hill exiting and then returning in a boot and on crutches raised more concern about the running back room. “Dierre was out this game, but I don't anticipate this being a long-term injury,” he said. “Obviously, we'll evaluate it. You know, everyone's different, so I have to get an update from our medical staff.” Lanning also delivered an update on defensive lineman Bear Alexander , who didn’t play in the second half after being listed as a game-time decision on the injury report. The Ducks’ coach went on to break down the performances of placekicker Gage Hurych and running back Simeon Price during his postgame press conference. “We were obviously playing a brand of football, trying to play keep-away in some ways, and a ton of respect for Coach Fitzgerald. But they were letting the clock tick down. We knew that we had to take advantage of opportunities to be able to go out there and score. I think once we kind of figured that out, the way we were able to play allowed us to go out there and show what I think we are, which is one of the best teams here down the stretch.” “And we always said we want to play our best ball in November. We walk away from that game. There's one drive on defense that I'm disappointed in. It was really about penalties, and then overall on offense, we were able to execute and really found some things there in the second half. I think we scored four out of the five drives in the second half.” “Obviously, kneeled it out there at the end, but some guys showed up for us as well. And our run game was really established. I think that was important in this game for that to be able to show up. But we played really clean second half, and we played. I thought we had some momentum there in the first. We're certainly an exciting team to watch.” “We got to clean up the penalties. That wasn't good enough, but to go score points six out of six trips into the red area, to be able to really do a better job on third down and really third and fourth downs on both sides of the ball in the second half I think was huge.” “So, giving our players the freedom to be able to say, ‘Hey, we're calling it, and if it's not there, you can check us out.’ And it wouldn't have been 100 percent. There is one look they have that looks very similar to what they were in that they could have popped out and maybe had some success.” “But I'm glad it was at, what was it the 15-yard line and not the 16, right? So, Gage has said, ‘If we ever call it, I'm going to score,’ and he did that today. So, it was awesome to see the guys go out there and execute and do it at a high level.” “Yeah, we were playing to win. Go, go, go! Score a touchdown. Obviously, once it went to review, if it was short, there was going to be two seconds left there on the clock, and we would have been able to have our offense out there ready to go on the ready whistle to go execut
